stem: Concerning hypermetropia
key: The eye is often shorter than the emmetropic eye
chosen: The near point distance decreases less than 10 cm
discriminator: Myopia: the image falls in front of the retina (long eyeball or too-strong refraction); the far point comes in to a finite distance and the near point sits closer than normal; corrected with a concave (diverging) lens. Hypermetropia: the image falls behind the retina (short eyeball); the eye must accommodate even for distance, so the near point RECEDES (farther than normal); corrected with a convex lens. Presbyopia: the lens loses elasticity with age and the near point recedes, so near vision needs a convex lens. Check each word of your option against this map: one detail is swapped.

stem: Regarding the cerebellar cortex, which of the following statements is true?
key: The dendrites of Golgi cells extend in all layers of the grey matter.
chosen: Granular cells have many long dendrites.
contrast: cerebellar_cells [Purkinje / Golgi / basket / stellate vs Granule cells]
discriminator: Cerebellar cortex cells: Purkinje cells are large flask-shaped neurons in a single row, with a flat, profusely branched dendritic tree in the molecular layer; they are the only output (GABA). Granule cells are tiny and packed in the granular layer, with 3–5 short claw-like dendrites; their axons ascend as parallel fibers (the only excitatory intrinsic cells). Golgi cells sit in the granular layer, and their dendrites reach up into the molecular layer. Basket and stellate cells lie in the molecular layer. Mossy fibers end on granule cells in glomeruli; climbing fibers wrap Purkinje dendrites.
felt: It is the nearest look-alike: same family, one different feature.

stem: Concerning Ventral spinocerebellar tract; which statement is correct
key: Cells of origin receive proprioceptive impulses from large cells in spinal ganglia.

discriminator: Conscious proprioception (position and vibration you can report) runs in the dorsal columns: DRG → gracile/cuneate nuclei → medial lemniscus → VPL thalamus → sensory cortex. The ventral tract crosses in the cord, enters by the superior peduncle and recrosses, so both end in the cerebellar half of their own side.
